doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Spirit in the music: Cecil McBee, Parker, Cannonball
summary: Responding to McBee's remark, Smith says real musicians play from their soul; he talks of Ellington, Parker and overlooking Cannonball for Trane.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: I had the pleasure of doing an interview with Cecil McBee.

What a wonderful guy. And I tried to ask a question. It had something to do with Charlie Parker and his generation and spirituality. And I guess I was asking him if the music of those masters from the 40s and so forth was less spiritual than things he was involved in with you and Pharoah. And I’m going to read what he said and ask for your comment on
it. He said “Well if it ain’t spiritual don’t play it. Your spirit is what makes you play the instrument.”

Oh that makes sense. Oh man, look at all those great things Duke Ellington did. And when I heard Charlie Parker playing “Just Friends” with strings I mean I couldn’t believe it. You know because I’m coming from a Gospel background and I heard all this beauty, oh no, the music was and is, I mean you know real music, and real creative music and real musicians they’re really playing from their inner being and their heart and their soul. I mean that’s automatically spiritual. Oh man, no, no indeed, they were definitely spiritual but they might not have said anything or talked about it but the music was fantastic.
Yes. Well I’m glad you said that and I think the reason one of my favorite musicians has always been Cannonball Adderley, and boy, he had some spirit.

Oh shucks, I mean Cannonball, because for a while there what was so in me, I was so busy listening to Trane I was overlooking Cannonball. Then later on I started listening to Cannonball on YouTube and everything. I said oh my goodness, I mean Cannonball was playing but I was so busy listening to Trane and oh man, shoot. Cannonball and that group he had with his brother, oh man.
